name: Greyish navy

sections.title: Greyish navy is a very dark, slightly warm blue carried into our library from the Japanese traditional color Kon, meaning simply "dark blue," and it sits 8.7 units from the plain [[navy]].
sections.body:
Our library lists this color under the Japanese name Kon, written 紺, glossed plainly as "dark blue" [1]. *Kon* is one of the oldest and most common dye names in Japan, historically tied to deep indigo dyeing, though our library's gloss does not itself specify indigo as the dyestuff, so that link is not asserted here [1].

The swatch measures lightness 13, chroma 15 and hue 281 degrees, in the Blues family, and it is nearly black at this lightness, used chiefly in fashion and textile contexts [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[mascot]], [[dark]], [[black-blue]] and [[trooper]], at 4.1, 4.1, 4.6 and 4.9 ΔE [1]. A darker green cousin in the same descriptive family is [[greyish-hunter-green]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: A color within range of this swatch appears in 193 of the 23,781 paintings in our archive, about 0.81 percent, as photographed, almost entirely in shadow areas [2]. The earliest dated match is Pietro Lorenzetti's 1340 *Madonna and Child Enthroned with Eight Angels*, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. The archive's photographs are of aged, varnished canvases, so a dark shadow match here is a screen color, not a dye or pigment identification [2].
